intent.purpose: The contract for deployment.json after the breaking redesign: a bundled, one-section-per-concern file that names the deployment's providers and its own model choices — defaultModel, decisionModel, escalationModel and visionModel — (with defaultAgent, timeZone and the exec policy for sessions), its stores and its services, its extensions and the core catalog, its notifications, its keyed services and its session driver configuration — without hand-listing models, which are discovered from each provider's /models endpoint when it exists; the hand-written model entries may carry cost fields (price, USD per million tokens) beside their limits.

nonGoals.text: Per-agent model choices, which are set in the UI and stored with the agent's config in the data dir
Secrets, which stay in the environment and are only named by *Env keys
The service roster and settings keys the owner has not fixed stay owned by the services' own contracts; github's and remarkable's are the fixed exception
External APIs' keys (exa, langfuse), which remain environment variables
Routing and auth of the /apps gateway, which is redrafted in the distributor.apps contract (session d87192eb) and deliberately not specified here

intent.audience: The operator who writes the deployment file, and the migration of prod's existing file.
consumers: The rewritten parseDeployment and buildModels in @quack/session
The distributor that rewrites the file per session
Each extension that now reads its configuration from the file, in-process
The distributor's parseHostConfig, which now reads the session section instead of the QUACK_SESSION_* environment

guarantees.text: A deployment with no hand-written models can boot from nothing but QUACK_DATA_DIR and this file
A bad defaultModel fails before deploy
Secrets never appear in the file
A typo'd store reference fails at load
A v6 file that still names extensions.index is refused with a message pointing at the root's catalog.store
github.settings' closed keys are exactly the ones the service reads; any other key is rejected and named
A v6 implementerAgent and label value in github.settings survive the migration unchanged
A model limit's price carries only input, output, cacheRead and cacheWrite, each a non-negative number of USD per million tokens
Planned (slice S4): a shipped agent bundle names no model
Planned: a bundle's models come from defaultModel, decisionModel, escalationModel and visionModel here, the agent's saved choice, and a turn's pick

document.title: Quack deployment (target shape)
document.description: The file QUACK_CONFIG points at: who a deployment may call (providers, with defaultModel, decisionModel, escalationModel and visionModel as the deployment's own model choices), where its data lives (stores), what services it runs (extensions), where its session catalog lives (catalog) and who web push is attributed to (notifications), which keyed outbound APIs the proxy fronts (services), and how sessions run (session); a new session starts with defaultAgent, and how its sessions behave (timeZone, exec). Models are not hand-listed here: they are discovered from each provider's GET {baseUrl}/models when that endpoint exists, and an agent's own model choice is set in the UI and stored with the agent's config in the data dir; a shipped agent bundle names none of them. The environment keeps only secrets, named here by *Env keys, and the process paths QUACK_DATA_DIR, QUACK_CONFIG and QUACK_AGENTS_DIR. One section per concern, in the spirit of v0's config/quack.yaml. The root is closed: an unknown top-level key — the removed imageModel and a typo alike — is rejected and named.

providers.description: The named providers sessions may call. A provider's hand-written models are optional: any model not listed there is discovered from GET {baseUrl}/models when that endpoint exists.

defaultModel.description: A "provider/model" reference: the model a new session runs on, the model for agents that have no saved choice, and the model a session returns to when the model a turn picked has left this file. A turn may pick any selectable model (session process API, Invocation.model) — planned in slice S5: the Invocation body carries input, requestId, wait, whenBusy, title and meta, and no model field yet. Each agent's saved choice is set in the UI (the Agents page) and stored with the agent's config in the data dir, so it is not in this file. defaultModel must resolve to a selectable model under the merge rule (one with a contextWindow); validate checks that before deploy, and selecting an unselectable model is an error when it happens.

timeZone.description: The IANA time zone session clocks run in; the default is America/New_York. It must be a zone the runtime's Intl accepts.

exec.description: How agent shells are confined; see execPolicy.

stores.description: Named stores; each consumer references one by name. A sqlite store keeps its file in the data dir, so a fresh install needs nothing provisioned; omit the section and every consumer falls back to its own default (a sqlite file in the data dir). Session logs stay files under the data dir, never a store.

extensions.description: The named extensions that mount in-process under /apps/<name>/* in the runtime/distributor — github, sleeper, remarkable, schedules and capacity are no longer separate services. Replaces the service database variables and the single-use setting variables; each extension's secrets are still read from the environment by name, declared in the extension's own manifest. An entry named slots is rejected as renamed — the extension and its app now mount at /apps/capacity, under the key extensions.capacity. An entry named index is refused — the catalog is core; name its store at the root's catalog.store instead. github and remarkable carry closed settings objects naming the keys the owner fixed; every other extension keeps the generic entry.

not.description: Refuses two entry names: index (the catalog is core; name its store at catalog.store) and slots (renamed to capacity), so the loader can name the right key in each case.

github.description: The GitHub extension: a closed settings object keeping every key the service reads — agent, label, appId, implementerAgent and issueBase — so /fix and branch basing do not break.

store.description: The name of a stores entry to hold this service's database; the loader checks the reference, and an absent store takes the service's default (a sqlite file in the data dir).

settings.description: The GitHub app's configuration, closed to the keys the service reads; any other key is rejected and named.

agent.description: The agent that backs unattended triggers, by name in the catalog; absent takes reviewer.

label.description: The review label the app applies; absent takes quack:review.

appId.description: The GitHub App's numeric id; the App's key file and the webhook secret remain environment secrets.

implementerAgent.description: The agent a trusted /fix comment runs; absent, /fix does nothing, so a deployment opts in by naming it. It must be promoted (DEP-6), checked by the loader like agent.

issueBase.description: The owner/repo to base a branch on.

remarkable.description: The remarkable extension: a closed settings object keeping every key the service reads — agent, url and email — the rmfakecloud endpoint it used to read from RMFAKECLOUD_URL and RMFAKECLOUD_EMAIL; the password stays an environment secret.

store.description: The name of a stores entry to hold this service's database; the loader checks the reference, and an absent store takes the service's default (a sqlite file in the data dir).

settings.description: The remarkable workflow's configuration, closed to the keys the service reads; the rmfakecloud password stays an environment secret.

agent.description: The agent the remarkable workflow runs, by name in the catalog; absent takes remarkable-ingest.

url.description: The rmfakecloud endpoint's base URL; replaces RMFAKECLOUD_URL.

email.description: The rmfakecloud account's email; replaces RMFAKECLOUD_EMAIL.

catalog.description: The core's session catalog: the name of a stores entry that holds it, checked against the stores map by the loader; an absent catalog (or an absent store) takes the default, a sqlite file in the data dir. The catalog is core, not an extension — it used to be read as the index service's database variable, so an extensions entry named index is refused with a message pointing here.

store.description: The name of a stores entry to hold the core's session catalog; the loader checks the reference, and an absent store takes the default (a sqlite file in the data dir).

notifications.description: The core's web-push contact, replacing the push configuration the deleted index service exposed as index.push; an absent section (or an absent subject) defaults to the quack repo URL. The VAPID keys are secrets and stay in the environment.

subject.description: The contact a web-push notification attributes (the VAPID link header); RFC 8292 requires a mailto: or https: URI, and anything else is rejected here with a clear error. Absent takes the quack repo URL, https://github.com/fagerbergj/quack.

services.description: The named keyed outbound APIs the key proxy registers, one per entry, under /proxy/<name>; extensions name the service they use instead of reading a per-service URL variable. Exa is one entry (exa: baseUrl https://api.exa.ai), not a special case; this replaces QUACK_EXA_URL, whose value moves to the exa entry's baseUrl. Langfuse is the other entry: its base URL replaces LANGFUSE_BASE_URL, and its basic-auth keys stay in the environment.

defaultAgent.description: The agent a new session starts with, by name in the core's session catalog; optional, absent taking the shipped home agent quack. When set, the loader checks it resolves to an installed agent, and a value that does not resolves fails to load.

session.description: The session driver configuration the distributor's parseHostConfig today reads from the QUACK_SESSION_* environment; a closed object, so a typo in a driver setting fails here with a named key. Absent takes the defaults — driver process, runsc, the quack-sessions network.

driver.description: How sessions run: process (the default, shells in the host's own process tree) or docker (one container per session, in which case the rest of this section applies).

image.description: The session container image (docker driver only).

runtime.description: The container runtime (docker driver only); runsc by default. runc shares the host kernel with the session's shell, which defeats the driver, and is refused unless allowRunc is true — dev and tests only. Recorded as the JSON Schema default; the distributor applies the same default.

network.description: The Docker network the session containers attach to (docker driver only); quack-sessions by default. Recorded as the JSON Schema default; the distributor applies the same default.

allowRunc.description: Lifts the refusal of runtime runc; true for dev and tests only, never in production.

distributorUrl.description: An http(s) URL the session containers can reach to call the distributor (docker driver only).

dataVolume.description: The Docker name of the named data volume the sessions mount; exactly one of dataVolume and hostDataDir — a named volume needs no migration but Docker Engine 26 or newer. The rule, enforced here: with driver docker exactly one of dataVolume and hostDataDir is set — both or neither fail with an error naming the rule; with driver process neither may be set.

hostDataDir.description: An absolute path on the Docker host holding session data; exactly one of dataVolume and hostDataDir.

driver.description: Match only the process driver, for which no data mount may be set.

else.description: The docker driver: image and distributorUrl are required and exactly one of dataVolume and hostDataDir is set — both or neither fail the oneOf with an error naming the rule; runtime and network are optional, taking their defaults.

decisionModel.description: The decision model the judge and workflow steps ask before any generation model, for agents whose extension config names none: a model of a systemone provider, whose contextWindow is its input cap. Absent: no default decision model; a check escalates unless the agent's config names one. validate and the loader refuse a reference that does not resolve, that names a provider which is not api systemone, or whose entry has no contextWindow to serve as the cap, and the message names this key, as for defaultModel. Planned: the loader fills this ref into the bundles that omit it.

escalationModel.description: The generation model the judge escalates an item to when no decision model settles it. It must resolve to a selectable generation model. Absent: defaultModel. It never follows a turn's model pick, so a verdict does not depend on the model a person chose for the session. Precedence: an agent's judge.judgeModel while that setting exists, then escalationModel, then defaultModel. validate and the loader refuse a reference that does not resolve to a selectable generation model, naming this key. Planned: the judge reading this key (slice S4 deletes judge.judgeModel).

visionModel.description: The model workflow steps read images with when the agent's config names none; it must declare images: true. Absent: the session's current model, which must then accept images — and a model that declares none is not sent them: pi-ai replaces the image blocks with a text placeholder before the request, so the step answers from the text alone. validate and the loader refuse a reference here that does not resolve, or resolves to a model without images: true, naming this key, as the workflows extension's own validator does for workflows.visionModel. Planned: the loader filling this ref for the agent's config.

baseUrl.description: The base URL of an OpenAI-compatible API; models are discovered from GET {baseUrl}/models when that endpoint exists. The distributor rewrites it to a per-session broker route, since a session container cannot reach the LAN.

api.description: The wire protocol. openai-completions is the default; systemone marks decision providers such as Clef — classifiers with an input cap and no generation.

apiKeyEnv.description: The name of the environment variable holding this provider's API key. When absent, the key is read from QUACK_<ID>_API_KEY, the provider id with non-alphanumerics upper-cased to underscores.

models.description: Hand-written model entries, keyed by model id. Merge rule: the provider's models are the ids discovered from GET {baseUrl}/models (when the endpoint exists) plus the hand-written ids here; a hand-written field wins over a discovered one, and a hand-written id the endpoint does not list is added. A model that ends up with no contextWindow is listed but cannot be selected; it is an error only when defaultModel or an agent selects it, so discovery never fails boot just because an endpoint is thin. For a provider with no /models endpoint this map is the whole model list. Measured on prod: llama.cpp upstreams add meta.n_ctx and architecture.input_modalities, while llm-swap (provider local) returns ids only — including peer models such as jaison/qwen3.8-27b — so contextWindow and images can still be written by hand even when discovery runs.

capacity.description: How many sessions this provider may serve at once through the capacity gate — a positive integer, one session is one holder, and one provider is one model endpoint. A provider without it is not gated. Renamed from slots: a file that still carries providers.<id>.slots is rejected at validation with a message naming the new key, as 'providers.local.slots was renamed to providers.local.capacity'; there is no silent alias, and after one release the special message may go and the old key falls to the ordinary unknown-key rejection.

not.description: The provider field slots is renamed to capacity; the schema rejects the old key so the loader can name the new one.

modelLimits.description: Hand-written limits for one model id; every field is optional here because what a provider needs written depends on what its GET {baseUrl}/models states, and a model with no contextWindow is listed but not selectable.

contextWindow.description: The context window in tokens; a model without one is listed but not selectable.

maxTokens.description: The longest one completion may be, in tokens.

reasoning.description: Whether this model takes reasoning effort parameters.

images.description: Whether this model takes image input; without it pi-ai replaces image blocks with a text placeholder before the request.

price.description: A notional price per million tokens; omitted parts are free.
A notional price per million tokens (power, say); omitted parts are free. pi-ai turns it into each call's `usage.cost`.

store.description: A named store. kind selects the adapter — the portability seam — so the set is closed: a new kind is a code change. The shape mirrors the SDK's AppStore: { kind: sqlite, path } or { kind: postgres, url via urlEnv }.

kind.description: Which adapter serves this store: sqlite keeps its file in the data dir (no other fields), postgres connects over the URL named by urlEnv.

urlEnv.description: The name of the environment variable holding the postgres connection URL; only for kind postgres, required when kind is postgres.

path.description: An absolute path to the sqlite file; kind sqlite only, an error otherwise; absent keeps the file in the data dir. Mirrors the SDK's AppStore, where a sqlite store is { kind: sqlite, path }.

kind.description: Match only stores of kind postgres.

execPolicy.description: How agent shells are confined; an agent may shorten the operator's timeout but never lengthen it.

timeoutSeconds.description: The longest one shell command may run, in seconds; the default is the session's default exec timeout.

env.description: Variable names the shell starts with, on top of the session's own environment.

limits.description: Kernel limits applied to shells via the limit prefix; an absent field keeps its default.

execLimits.description: Kernel limits the session applies to shells via the limit prefix; an absent field keeps its default.

maxFileSizeMb.description: The largest one file may grow to, in megabytes; the default is 1024.

extension.description: One extension's configuration: an optional store for its database and an optional settings object. The extension mounts in-process under /apps/<name>/* in the runtime/distributor, so nothing calls another process and the entry carries no url or tokenEnv; routing and auth are the /apps gateway's concern, redrafted in the distributor.apps contract, and not specified here.

store.description: The name of a stores entry to hold this service's database; the loader checks the reference, and an absent store takes the service's default (a sqlite file in the data dir).

settings.description: Service-owned settings, replacing that service's single-use environment variables (for example QUACK_RETENTION_SWEEP, QUACK_GH_IMPLEMENTER_AGENT, QUACK_SLEEPER_OWNER and QUACK_SLEEPER_LEAGUE). The shape is owned by the extension and defined in the extension's own contract — v1 core is the harness plus generic hooks, so the generic entry hard-codes no keys; the only exceptions are github and remarkable, whose owner-fixed closed settings live on sibling properties of the extensions object. It is checked twice: once by validate before deploy, using the extension's published validator (as agent extensions already work through CatalogEntry.validate), and again by the extension when the process boots. Secrets an extension needs — the GitHub App key file and webhook secret, the rmfakecloud password — are still read from the environment by name, declared in the extension's manifest, and never written here.

keyedService.description: One keyed outbound API the key proxy fronts: it registers under /proxy/<name> and extensions name the service they use, so no service is a special case in core. Today core hard-codes Exa here; this map is that registration, generalized. Exa and langfuse are its entries; today core hard-codes both registrations here.

baseUrl.description: The base URL the proxy dials for this service; required, since unlike providers the proxy cannot discover it.

apiKeyEnv.description: The name of the environment variable holding this service's API key. When absent, the key is read from QUACK_<NAME>_API_KEY, the service name upper-cased; the key itself never appears in the file.

choices.decision: deployment.json is an object with required providers and defaultModel and optional timeZone, exec, stores and services — one section per concern: who it calls, its fallback model, where its data lives, what it runs, and how sessions behave; the hand-written model registry, imageModel and the single-use top-level keys go away, replaced by /models discovery and the stores/services sections. Note: this revision is the one the approved environment contract (contracts:0c200fa8 v4) names deployment.json v9, because the rejected drafts consumed that number, so a reader following the env contract finds it there. The v0 reference config/quack.yaml is no longer on main, so its cited lines no longer resolve.

why.text: New direction from the owner: this contract is a breaking redesign, not a description of today's loader — design the target shape, with one migration of prod's file, and do not keep legacy keys valid. Models come from each provider's /models endpoint, map to agents via a default model or per-agent UI config, and stores and services get bundled sections; v0's config/quack.yaml is the reference for what good bundling felt like.

Rejected on one defect: the docker branch requires runtime and network, but both are documented with defaults (runsc; quack-sessions) and the distributor applies them (host-config.ts:26 and :38), so a docker config relying on them would fail to load. Require only image and distributorUrl plus exactly one data mount; keep runtime and network optional with their defaults, and record the defaults as JSON Schema default values. Also add one sentence to the choices: this revision is the one the approved environment contract (contracts:0c200fa8 v4) names deployment.json v9, because rejected drafts consumed that number.

choices.decision: The top level is closed (additionalProperties false): validate rejects any unknown top-level key — the removed imageModel and a typo alike — and names it, so a legacy key cannot validate silently.

why.text: Close the root instead (additionalProperties: false) and drop the not clause, so validate rejects any unknown top-level key, the removed imageModel and typos alike, and names it. Service settings stay free-form inside services, per answer 356.

Every property has a description that says what it means and its unit, not its type.

choices.decision: A provider may name capacity, a positive integer: how many sessions the capacity gate lets it serve at once; a provider without it is not gated. It replaces the field slots, renamed with the extension whose app now mounts at /apps/capacity, and it keeps the place the old QUACK_SLOTS_LIMITS endpoint map had, because the limit belongs with the provider it limits. For one release, a file that still carries providers.<id>.slots is rejected at validation with a message naming the new key — for example 'providers.local.slots was renamed to providers.local.capacity'; there is no silent alias, and after one release the special message may go and the old key falls to the ordinary unknown-key rejection. The rename has landed in the code, which now spells the key capacity in capacityLimits, in the provider validation and in the SDK's DeploymentFile type, and the extension itself is packages/capacity.

Issue #2462 slice S4, deployment v15 to v16: deployment-level decision, escalation and vision models, so shipped agent bundles stop naming the owner's models. Three additive optional root properties (decisionModel, escalationModel, visionModel) with the owner's exact descriptions, defaultModel's description reworded, the guarantee 'A shipped agent bundle names no model: its models come from defaultModel, decisionModel, escalationModel and visionModel here, from the agent's saved choice, and from a turn's pick', and the compatibility note that all three keys are optional and new so a v15 file is a valid v16 file and runs as before, except that the judge escalates to defaultModel instead of the session's own model. Implementation follows approval: the loader fills refs bundles omit, the judge escalates to escalationModel else defaultModel. On prod this is behaviour-neutral: every agent already runs on defaultModel and decisionModel will be clef/clef with contextWindow 8192.

changes.was: defaultModel was 'the model for agents that do not choose one of their own'.
changes.now: The same required property, reworded: the model a new session runs on, the model for agents with no saved choice, and the model a session returns to when the model a turn picked has left the file, with a turn free to pick any selectable model through the session process API's Invocation.model — marked planned, slice S5, since the Invocation body has no model field yet.
changes.why: Slice S4 states defaultModel's whole role; the turn's pick is S5's code, so it is marked planned rather than presented as today's behaviour.

changes.was: v15 had no deployment-level decision model; each bundle carried its own judge.decisionModel, so a shipped bundle named the owner's Clef ref.
changes.now: An optional decisionModel — a 'provider/model' string naming a systemone model whose contextWindow is its input cap; absent, no default decision model and a check escalates unless the agent's config names one; validate and the loader refuse a reference that does not resolve or names the wrong kind of model, and name the key.
changes.why: So shipped agent bundles stop naming the owner's models; the loader fills the ref a bundle omits, which is planned, not yet code.

changes.was: v15 had no deployment-level escalation model; with judge.judgeModel unset the judge escalated an uncertain item to the agent's own model, following the session's pick.
changes.now: An optional escalationModel, a selectable generation model; absent, defaultModel. Precedence: judge.judgeModel while it exists, then escalationModel, then defaultModel. It never follows a turn's model pick.
changes.why: A verdict must not depend on the model a person chose for the session; RFC 0002 deletes judgeModel in slice S4.

changes.was: v15 had no deployment-level vision model; workflow steps read images with the session's current model, or the agent's own workflows.visionModel.
changes.now: An optional visionModel that must declare images: true; absent, the session's current model, which must then accept images — one that declares none is not sent them, so the step answers from the text alone.
changes.why: The image-reading model is a deployment choice, not a bundle choice; the no-images behaviour is stated instead of left implicit.

changes.was: Only defaultModel named a model as 'provider/model'.
changes.now: The three new refs use defaultModel's pattern and the loader's split; the kind each must resolve to is checked by validate and at load, which name the offending key.
changes.why: One way of naming a model across the file, and the edge cases are refused rather than surfacing later as a generation failure.

changes.was: The full example carried every v15 optional field, and its clef provider declared no models.
changes.now: It also carries decisionModel clef/clef, escalationModel local/qwen3.8-flash-next and visionModel local/qwen3-omni-30b, and declares the models those refs name — clef with contextWindow 8192, and local/qwen3.8-flash-next with contextWindow 262144 and maxTokens 32768 — so the example's refs resolve.

breaking.what: An escalation verdict changes for any agent whose model differs from defaultModel: today, with judge.judgeModel unset, an uncertain item is asked of the agent's own model; from this version it is asked of escalationModel, or of defaultModel when that key is absent. Prod is unaffected today: neither key is set there and every agent runs on defaultModel, so the escalation target is the model it already uses.
callers: the deployment files on prod and QA
breaking.migration: Set escalationModel to the model verdicts should settle on, or keep judge.judgeModel per agent until slice S4 deletes it.

breaking.what: Rollout: the root is closed, so a deployment file carrying decisionModel, escalationModel or visionModel is refused by v15 code as an unknown top-level key.
callers: the deployment files on prod and QA
breaking.migration: Ship the loader that reads the three keys before the prod and QA files gain them, and remove the keys from those files before rolling the code back.

safe: All three keys are optional and new; a v15 file is a valid file of this version and, for a deployment where every agent already runs on defaultModel, runs as before.
defaultModel's constraint is unchanged — required, a 'provider/model' string that must resolve to a selectable model before deploy; only its description is reworded.
No key was removed, renamed, made required, or narrowed: the root's required list is still providers and defaultModel, and the root stays closed.

The per-agent extension configs keep working: a bundle or agent config that names judge.decisionModel, judge.judgeModel or workflows.visionModel still wins over the deployment default, so an existing bundle behaves as it does today until the ref is dropped from it.

The two not clauses are refusals, not requirements: not.required names the old 'slots' key (a provider's, and an extensions entry named slots) and extensions.index, so a file carrying them is rejected with a message naming the new key; nothing in this schema requires slots.
